name: olai-plugin-identity
//name: UNSCOPED, like every other row. `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai; this one is a plugin the loader mounts by name off a row in `packages/bundle/olai.yml`. It was `@olai/identity`, a general leaf package, until who is looking became a door core defines and a row stands behind. The directory is `packages/plugins/identity` and the package name is `olai-plugin-identity`.
//exports: Server reading, browser chip, wire identity, test identifiers and stylesheet. Shared person rendering lives in @olai/web/client/who.
//: WHO IS LOOKING, as a row. A login the reverse proxy injected, or nobody; the picture ladder that decides what that person wears; and the chip in the top right that draws the answer. Core defines the `Identity` door and reads it at the upgrade, at `GET /olai/who` and at `/mcp`; this row is what stands behind it.
//dependencies: `@olai/plugin-api` is the door: the `Offers` tag the server half stands behind `Identity` with, the `Env` it reads the operator's family out of, and the `Slots` its chip hangs in. `effect` because a plugin's `apply` is one. `solid-js` because the chip is a component. `@olai/surface` for the `Who` schema the tab's ask is typed by — the SAME value core's `who.get` answers with, so the chip cannot draw a shape the server does not send; type-only in the browser half, and no runtime of it reaches the reading. `@olai/web` is the shell door every browser half opens for the app's own furniture (the icon button, the tip, the layer). NOTHING under `./who`: the reading is a function of the arguments it is handed, which is what lets a test state a deployment instead of arranging one, and `node:crypto` is a builtin.
//devDependencies: @olai/format for ONE refusal class in ONE test — the shape a procedure fails with, so the test that says a failed ask is a THROW rather than honest absence fails with the failure the wire really carries. A devDependency and not a runtime one, deliberately: the chip draws a person or a silhouette and never a vault record, and this row is the one plugin in the tree whose faces read nothing of the format at all.
